text: This story stands up the deviation slice of the sandbox as the `deviation-seed` module of `tools/sandbox-generator` in the rwb-deviation repository, run by the same DEV stage contract as RWB-P1-E1065-CON, writing `deviation` rows in `rwb_deviation` of its own `rwb_sandbox` database; the case references a deviation attaches to, their product group, their exception shape and the routed state they paused in come from the case-reference fixture of the seed profile and never from a read of `rwb_case` or `recovery_case`.
why: Legacy RWB-E1-065 seeds every table of one `recovery` schema from one project, and the target gives one schema and one owner per service with no cross-service table read (DP-01, DP-02); the case estate belongs to rwb-case and the interaction ledger to rwb-source-data, so the deviation rows can only be attached to references the owner of the case estate publishes, which the seed profile is the natural place for.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 2, 4 and 11; context pack S8 ownership rows; Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 (DP-01); RWB-P1-E1065-APP sections 3 and 11 (one sandbox per service release, the deviation rows handed to this story); TSD S8 T3.3 (deviation many to 1 recovery_case)
applied_in: RWB-S8-E1065-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 5 X8, 7 AC1 and AC4, 11, 12.2, 12.7, 12.8 and 13
confirm: Solution architect and the sandbox owner of rwb-source-data, before the stage contract is tagged
impact: The seed has no row without the fixture; if the fixture is not published, the deviation slice cannot be built and the wave 1 exit reports the gap

text: The dictionary rows of `deviation` and the three lists LOV-DEVIATION (X1 to X7), LOV-RAISED-BY and LOV-DEV-OUTCOME are seeded with the per-service baseline in the sandbox, and the seeder reads them there at the version in force; DP-07 applies as a rule of the seed and not as a call, so the C row of DP-07 (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) is not taken and this story makes no runtime call to rwb-case.
why: The three lists are published as this service's own rows in TSD S8 T3.2 and the dictionary is the source of every generated value (legacy BR3), while the plan's C row for this secondary slice holds only RWB-P1-E1065-CON; a build that called rwb-case for its own lists would add a contract dependency the plan does not carry and would fail closed on a SIT outage.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 BR2, BR3 and section 11 (DF-REF-027 to DF-REF-029, DF-REF-097 to DF-REF-105); TSD S8 T3.2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-07) and R7.3; split plan RWB-S8-E1065-APP (C RWB-P1-E1065-CON)
applied_in: RWB-S8-E1065-APP sections 3, 4 step 4, 5 X7, 7 AC2 and AC3, 8 BR3, 11, 12.2, 12.8 and 13
confirm: Data steward and the rwb-case reference-data owner, before the wave 1 entry check
impact: The seed fails closed on a missing list instead of inventing a value; the lists and the dictionary move with the service's own migrations

text: The platform libraries that DP-03, DP-04, DP-15 and DP-19 name (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) arrive with the service template, so the metadata rows stay H = None and C = RWB-P1-E1065-CON as the Work Package fixes them; the stage contract read is the only consumed operation, its operation and field names beyond the four rows of section 12.2 are not published, and DP-04's C row RWB-P7-E1073-CON is not taken because the smoke check evaluates the package held in its own fixture.
why: The plan's H row for this secondary slice is empty while the pattern set carries four patterns whose DP table rows add a platform H dependency, and the build reads one contract once per build; no source names the operation or the fields of that read.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-03, DP-04, DP-15, DP-19), R5.7; split plan story line RWB-S8-E1065-APP (H empty, C RWB-P1-E1065-CON); legacy RWB-E1-065 section 12
confirm: Platform library owner and the rwb-source-data sandbox owner, before the wave 1 entry check
impact: The slice builds on Day 1 on the template; a missing library blocks the decision record or the smoke check but not the seed of the rows

text: The seeder writes one open deviation per shaped case reference of the fixture: X3 for the deceased shape with contact_stop true and with the return point the fixture gives, X5 for the bankruptcy shape, and a code from LOV-DEVIATION for the open-deviation shape, with X1, X2, X4, X6 and X7 covered by the estate so every code of the list in force has at least one open row; one row per case is the reading, because no source publishes a deviation count per case.
why: Legacy BR4 fixes 10 cases per exception shape and only three of the ten shapes are deviations, while the deviation service and the rules of the DEV route set cover all seven codes; the number of deviations a case carries, the count per code and the shape-to-code mapping beyond X3 and X5 are not published, so a count is chosen and recorded rather than invented in silence.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 BR4 and BR5 (DL15, DL16); FSD S8 A2.5 (contact stop for X1 to X3), A2.12 (X3 deceased), A2.14 (X5 bankruptcy); Architecture v5 slide 8; TSD S8 T3.2 and T4
applied_in: RWB-S8-E1065-APP sections 4 steps 5 and 6, 7 AC2 and AC4, 8 BR4, 9 and 11
confirm: Business lead of S8 and the rule-set owner of the Deviations package, before the seed profile is signed off
impact: A changed count or mapping is a property and a fixture change, not a code change; if the volumes of the case estate change, the shaped references follow the fixture

text: Each seeded open deviation is written in state DEV_FLAGGED, the state R-DEV-01 leads to, and its owner from R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 is projected and compared in the smoke check rather than written; the local decision record of a seeded raise names R-DEV-01 and the package version in force, and its decision code is the code of the raise story that owns the action, because no source publishes a decision code for a seeded row.
why: TSD S8 T4 gives DEV_FLAGGED as the target of R-DEV-01 from any state and gives the owner transitions as separate events, so a seeded row that jumped to DEV_WITH_OWNER would assert a transition no signal produced; the decision code of a raise is not printed by any source read.
read: TSD S8 T4 (R-DEV-01 ANY_STATE to DEV_FLAGGED, R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 to DEV_WITH_OWNER); FSD S8 A2.2.3.1; legacy RWB-E1-065 section 11 (decision_log_entry receives its rows from running the jobs)
applied_in: RWB-S8-E1065-APP sections 4 steps 6 to 8, 7 AC8, 8 and 9
confirm: Rule-set owner of the Deviations package and the rwb-decision contract owner
impact: The smoke check proves the route set against the seeded rows without asserting a state only a live signal produces

text: The read-only role of the sandbox and its grant are the stage contract's (C RWB-P1-E1065-CON) and are created by the sandbox DB story RWB-P1-E1065-DB; this story asserts the grant on `rwb_deviation` and on `deviation` and creates neither the role nor a grant, and the DB story is outside this story's empty X row as the Work Package fixes it.
why: The legacy story creates the role and the grant in its own pipeline step, but in the target one story owns a database object and one story tests it; the plan gives this slice no X row, so the ownership is stated in the assumption and in the section 10 authority table rather than asserted as a dependency.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4 step 10, 10 and 13; RWB-P1-E1065-CON AC3 (three schemas, one read-only role, DEV only); split plan RWB-S8-E1065-APP (X empty)
confirm: ACE DB team lead and the rwb-source-data sandbox owner, before the stage contract is tagged
impact: The extraction test of AC6 fails until the DB story delivers the role; the seed and the verifier are unaffected

text: The ten legacy test cases keep their IDs and their Covers and Data carried onto the deviation slice, each naming the half this story answers; the legacy level System maps to End to end because the stage spans schemas and fixtures and Access maps to Component, as in the other sandbox slices of this run.
why: The legacy table publishes no level and the test cases are shared by five slices of the key, so a level has to be assigned and the ownership of each half stated; the other E1065 slices of this run use the same mapping, which keeps the Test Cases master consistent.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 16; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 (s16); the sibling sandbox stories RWB-P1-E1065-APP and RWB-P3-E1065-APP
confirm: QA lead, before the first wave 1 exit
impact: A revised level or split is a Test Cases master change and not a story change

text: The seeded deviation estate is shown on the deviation screens SCR-06 and SCR-08 through the service in DEV, merged by the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19, and this story builds no screen and fixes no screen state.
why: The legacy story builds no screen either (legacy section 15), and in the target a screen is a route of the gateway-bff and a state of the story that owns the screen; the seeded rows only make those states demonstrable.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 15; Architecture v5 slide 8 (Recovery gateway-bff); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-19)
confirm: Solution architect and the gateway-bff contract owner
impact: No screen work is estimated here; the screen stories of S8 test against the seeded estate

text: Because the dictionary tags no `deviation` column `is_personal`, the verifier scans every text column of `rwb_deviation` for the national ID pattern with a valid check digit, a mobile number and an email, and every column the dictionary tags on any table of the schema; a clear identity number in schema `public` is not a failure, because ACE holds it and this service reads no ACE table.
why: Legacy AC7 scans the columns tagged `is_personal` and legacy BR9 confines a clear identity number to the ACE-shaped tables, but the deviation table has no tagged column, so the check would pass trivially and prove nothing about the one field that names a person (`handler_user_id`).
read: Legacy RWB-E1-065 AC7, BR1, BR9 and section 11; TSD S8 T3.1 and T3.0; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 (s17)
applied_in: RWB-S8-E1065-APP sections 4 step 9, 7 AC7, 8 BR9, 11, 13 and 17
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer with the data steward, before the verifier is signed off
impact: A wider scan fails a build that a tagged-column scan would pass, which is the safe direction; a narrower scope needs a dictionary tag and a new migration
